ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage regulator circuit with CW7809 as the core, and the input terminal is marked 24V. The right side of the output terminal is labeled U0, and is connected to a voltage-divider branch made of R1, Rp, and R2 in series: R1=10kΩ, Rp=5kΩ, R2=10kΩ. The common terminal of CW7809 is connected to the potentiometer Rp through the sliding contact; when the sliding contact of Rp is adjusted to the lowest end, the common terminal is equivalently connected at the junction between Rp and R2. Reasoning: At this time, the resistance above from the output terminal to the common terminal is R1+Rp=10kΩ+5kΩ=15kΩ, and the lower resistance from the common terminal to ground is R2=10kΩ. Let the output voltage with respect to ground be U0, then the common-terminal voltage is Uc=U0×10/(15+10)=0.4U0. CW7809 maintains 9V from the output terminal relative to the common terminal, so U0−Uc=9V, namely U0−0.4U0=9V, 0.6U0=9V, solving gives U0=15V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, when the sliding contact of the potentiometer \(R_p\) is adjusted to the lowest end, what is the output voltage \(U_0\)?

method.method_draft: First identify from the image that when the Rp slider is at the lowest end, the regulator common pin is tied to the junction between Rp and R2. Therefore the divider from output to ground has R1+Rp=15 kΩ above the common node and R2=10 kΩ below it. Let the output voltage to ground be U0. The common-node voltage is U0·10/(10+5+10)=0.4U0, while the 7809 requires U0 minus this common-node voltage to equal 9 V. Solve 0.6U0=9 V to get U0=15 V.

method.method_draft: First read the resistor connections in the figure and set the slider at the lowest end, making the 15 kΩ section between output and the regulator common pin. Since the CW7809 holds 9 V across that 15 kΩ section, the divider current is 9 V / 15 kΩ = 0.6 mA. The lower resistor R2=10 kΩ then has a drop of 0.6 mA·10 kΩ = 6 V from the common pin to ground. Add the regulated 9 V above the common pin and the 6 V lift of the common pin above ground, giving U0=15 V.
